Norms for empanelment of ODR Institutions by MIs and continuing obligations of ODR Institutions 

MIs role and responsibility: 


1. An MII shall empanel one or more ODR Institutions as a service provider and enter into relevant agreements with 
such ODR Institution(s) in accordance with guidelines issued by the Board on outsourcing of activities by stock exchanges, 
depositories and clearing corporations (as amended from time to time) and this circular. An MII should ensure that the 
primary/first ODR Institution to be empaneled with it, is not empaneled as the primary/first ODR Institution with any other 
MII. 


2. An MII shall collect requisite information of a ODR Institution desirous of being empaneled for providing ODR 
services for the Indian Securities Market. Such information shall include: copies of registration certificate, memorandum of 
association and articles of association/ constitutional documents, rules governing conciliation and arbitration, PAN, Legal 
Entity Identifier number, composition of its board of directors, governing bodies and advisory councils, if any, and details of 
its shareholders and investors, and list of its authorised officials / signatories. Changes if any to any of these may be notified 
to the concerned MII promptly. An MII may drop an ODR Institution from its panel, if there is a delay in notifying or if the 
changes are viewed by the concerned MII as not conducive to continuance of the ODR institution on the panel. 


3. An ODR Institution shall also furnish other credentials that are deemed relevant to the empanelment process 
including: details of conciliators and arbitrators empanelled by the ODR Institution, norms for such empanelment, fees, costs 
and charges levied for conduct of online conciliation and arbitration, institutional/corporate clients or other ecosystems where 
rendering online conciliation and arbitration, aggregate number of disputes received for resolution whether for online 
conciliation or arbitration, aggregate number of disputes resolved by means of online conciliation and arbitration, aggregate 
value of disputes resolved by means of online conciliation and arbitration, types and nature of disputes resolved by mean of 
online conciliation and arbitration, technologies, platform, platform features and facilities in conducting online conciliation 
and arbitration. Such credentials shall be furnished at the time of empanelment and thereafter on a quarterly basis 
(April/July/October/January). 


4. The details of conciliators and arbitrators required to be furnished shall include: unique count of conciliators and 
arbitrators trained in the securities market, along with the education, training and professional qualification, number of years of 
experience, previous experience in conciliation / arbitration including experience in specific types, natures or sectors, 
languages conversant with (spoken/written) and other demographic details such as age, sex, location. 


5. MIIs shall ensure that the ODR Institutions eligible for empanelment have the ability to integrate their own 
platform/systems with the ODR Portal for requirements and purposes as specified from time to time, and on or prior to 
empanelment undertake necessary integration. MIIs shall also ensure that the ODR Institutions also have sufficient 
technologies to ensure due secrecy, confidentiality and cyber-security for the dataflow between the ODR Portal and its 
platform/systems, collection of fees and charges (or its refund) and for the conduct of online conciliation and arbitration. 
MIls shall also ensure the ODR Institution deploys and makes available such features or facilities on its platform/systems as 
required by the Board from time to time. 


6. MIIs shall ensure that the ODR Institution and its conciliators and arbitrators abide by the Code of Conduct 
(Schedule E) and highest standards of independence, impartiality, ethics and confidentiality as befits conciliation and 
arbitration, and interests of Indian Securities Market and with the applicable laws including the Arbitration and Conciliation 
Act, 1996.

members MII empaneled ODR Institutions for the Indian Securities Market on or before October 31, 2023. Details of such 
association / trade body shall be furnished to the MIIs and the Board, and shall include: copies of registration certificate, 
memorandum of association and articles of association/ constitutional documents, PAN, Legal Entity Identifier number, 
composition of its board of directors, governing bodies and advisory councils, if any, and details of its members, and list of 
its authorised officials / signatories. Such association / trade body shall undertake such activities and perform such roles and 
responsibilities as may be specified from time to time.

MINISTRY OF PERSONNEL, PUBLIC GRIEVANCES AND PENSIONS 
(Department of Personnel and Training) 


New Delhi, the 9th September, 2024 
G.S.R. 124.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution, the 
President, hereby makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to the post of Administrative Officer 
in the Central Bureau of Investigation, under the Ministry of Personnel, Public Grievances and Pensions, Department of 
Personnel and Training, namely:- 
1. Short title and commencement. - (1) These rules may be called the Ministry of Personnel, Public, Grievances 


and Pensions, Department of Personnel and Training, Central Bureau of Investigation, Administrative 
Officer (Group-‘A’ Posts) Recruitment Rules, 2024. 


(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 
2. Application. - These rules shall apply to the posts specified in column(1) of the Schedule annexed to these rules. 


3. | Number of posts, Classification and level in pay matrix. - The number of said posts, its classification and pay 
level in the pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the said Schedule. 


4. Methods of recruitment, age-limit and qualifications, etc. - The method of recruitment, age-limit, 
qualifications and other matters relating to the said posts shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the 
aforesaid Schedule. 


5.  Disqualifications. - No person, 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 
shall be eligible for appointment to the said post: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal law 
applicable to such person and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, 
exempt any person from the operation of this rule. 


6. Power to relax. - Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it 
may, by order, for reasons to be recorded in writing and in consultation with the Union Public Service 
Commission, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class or category of persons. 


7. Saving. - Nothing in these rules shall affect reservations, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions required to 
be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Other Backward Classes, Ex-servicemen and 
other special category of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to 
time in this regard.

G.S.R. 125.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution, and in 
supersession of (i) the Central Drugs Testing Laboratory, Chennai (Junior Scientific Assistant) Recruitment Rules, 
2001, (ii) the Central Drugs Testing Laboratory, Chennai, Senior Scientific Assistant, Recruitment Rules, 2004, (iii) the 
Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Central Drugs Testing Laboratory, Chennai (Group ‘A’ Posts) Recruitment 
Rules, 2004, and (iv) the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Directorate General of Health Services, (Director, 
Central Drugs Testing Laboratory, Chennai) Recruitment Rules, 2013, except as respects things done or omitted to be 
done before such supersession, the President hereby makes the following rules regulating the method of recruitment to 
the posts of Director, Senior Scientific Officer, Scientific Officer, Senior Scientific Assistant and Junior Scientific 
Assistant in the Central Drugs Testing Laboratory, Chennai, Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation, Directorate 
General of Health Services, Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, namely:- 


1. Short title and commencement. - (1) These rules may be called the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, 
Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation, Director, Senior Scientific Officer, Scientific Officer, Senior Scientific 
Assistant and Junior Scientific Assistant, Central Drugs Testing Laboratory, Chennai, (Group ‘A’ and ‘B’ posts) 
Recruitment Rules, 2024. 

(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 


2. Application. - These rules shall apply to the posts as specified in column (1) of the Schedule annexed to these 
rules. 


3. Number of posts, classification and level in pay matrix. - The number of the said posts, their classification and 
level in the pay matrix attached thereto shall be as specified in columns (2) to (4) of the said Schedule.

4. Method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications, etc.- The method of recruitment, age-limit, qualifications and 
other matters relating to the said posts shall be as specified in columns (5) to (13) of the Said Schedule. 


5. Disqualification. - No person, - 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 


(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any other person, shall be eligible for 
appointment to the said posts: 


Provided that the Central Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal 
law applicable to such persons and other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt 
any person from the operation of this rule. 


6. Power to relax. - Where the Central Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it 
may, by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing and in consultation with the Union Public Service 
Commission, relax any of the provisions of these rules with respect to any class or category of persons. 


7. Savings. - Nothing in these rules shall affect reservation, relaxation of age-limit and other concessions required to 
be provided for the Scheduled Castes, the Scheduled Tribes, the Other Backward Classes, the Ex- servicemen and 
other special categories of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Central Government from time to time 
in this regard.

S.R.O. 52.—In exercise of powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution and in 
supersession of the Defence Research and Development Organisation Technical Cadre Recruitment Rules, 2000, 
except as respects things done or omitted to be done before such supersession, the President hereby makes the 
following rules regulating the method of recruitment to Group ‘A’, Group ‘B’ and Group ‘C’ technical posts in the 
Defence Research and Development Organisation, Ministry of Defence, namely: — 


l. Short title and commencement.—(]) These rules may be called the Ministry of Defence, Defence Research 
and Development Organisation Technical Cadre Recruitment Rules, 2024. 
(2) They shall come into force on the date of their publication in the Official Gazette. 

2. Definitions.—In these rules, unless the context otherwise requires,— 

(a) “Assessment Board” means a Board constituted under sub-rules (l) and (4) of rule 5; 

(b) “cadre” means Defence Research Technical Cadre; 

(c) “category” means category of the cadre; 

(d) “Chairperson, DRDO” means the Chairperson of the Defence Research and Development 

Organisation; 

(e) “Government” means the Government of India; 

(f) “grade” means a grade of the cadre; 

(g) “Schedule” means schedule annexed to these rules; and 

(h) “Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes” shall have the same meanings as assigned to them 


respectively in clauses (24) and (25) of article 366 of the Constitution. 


362 THE GAZETTE OF INDIA : SEPTEMBER 2], 2024/BHADRA 30, [946 [PART II—SEc. 4] 


3. Categories, grades, authorised strength and its review.—(l) The posts and grades included in the cadre, 
their Level in pay matrix and classification shall be as specified in the First Schedule. 
(2) Authorised permanent strength of the various categories in the cadre shall be such as may, from time 
to time, be determined by the Government. 
(3) The Government may make temporary additions to or deletions from the strength of various 
categories as deemed necessary from time to time. 
(4) The Government may include in the cadre any post other than those included in the First Schedule 
or exclude from the cadre a post included in the said Schedule. 
(5) The Government may appoint any officer whose post is included in the cadre under sub-rule (4), to 
the appropriate grade of the cadre in a temporary capacity or in a substantive capacity, as it may be deemed 
fit. 
(6) Notwithstanding anything contained in the foregoing sub-rules, the authorised strength of category- 


B shall, at no time, exceed sixty per cent. of the total authorised strength of the cadre. 


4. Future maintenance.—(l) All new posts shall be created only in the lowest grades of category-A and 
category-B as specified in the First Schedule. 


(2) Vacancies in any grade due to retirement, resignation etc. shall revert to the post of Technician ‘A’ 
in category-A and to the post of Senior Technical Assistant ‘B’ in category —B in the ratio of 40:60, subject 
to the sanctioned strength of posts in each category. 


(3) No vacancy shall arise in a grade on promotion of a person from that grade to the next higher grade 
and on promotion from one grade to the next grade, the post held by an individual in the lower grade shall 
stand upgraded automatically and shall be personal to the individual. 


(4) Direct Recruitment: (a) Direct recruitment shall be made only in the lowest grades of category-A 
and category-B for which the qualifications and age limits shall be as laid down in the Second Schedule. 


(b) Candidates possessing the higher qualifications viz., Master of Science, Doctor of Philosophy, Bachelor 
of Technology, Bachelor of Engineering Degrees etc. in any subject or discipline shall not be considered for 
recruitment to both categories. 


(c) Candidates with Diploma or Bachelor’s Degree in Science shall be eligible for recruitment to the lowest 
grade of category-A provided such candidates fulfil the educational qualification requirements for 
recruitment to the lowest grade of category-A, as laid down in the Second Schedule. 


(5) Departmental Competitive Examination (DCE): (a) Fifty per cent. of the vacancies for 
recruitment in the lowest grade of category-A and twenty-five per cent. of the vacancies in the lowest grade 
of category-B shall be filled through Departmental Competitive Examination from amongst departmental 
employees with minimum three years regular service in Defence Research and Development Organisation 
and possessing qualifications prescribed in the Second Schedule but without any age limit, failing which the 
unfilled vacancies may be filled by direct recruitment. 


(b) Possession of higher qualifications like Master of Science, Doctor of Philosophy, Bachelor of 
Technology, Bachelor of Engineering degrees etc. by departmental candidates is not a bar for appearing to 
recruitment to the lowest grades of category-A and category-B through Departmental Competitive 
Examination, provided such candidates possess the qualifications prescribed in the Second Schedule for 
recruitment to that grade. 


(6) For filling up the posts through direct recruitment or through Departmental Competitive 
Examination, the choice of specialisations, subject to sub-rules (4) and (5), shall be at the discretion of the 
appointing authority depending upon the functional requirement. 


(7) The composition of the Selection Board for direct recruitment or recruitment through Departmental 
Competitive Examination to the lowest grades of category-A and category-B is as given in the Fourth 
Schedule. 


5. Limited Flexible Complementing Scheme.—(]) (a) Promotions from one grade to another grade shall be 
made under the merit-based Limited Flexible Complementing Scheme, from amongst eligible personnel in the cadre 
and the names of the eligible candidates are recommended by Eligibility Screening Committee for Defence Research 
Technical Cadre Assessment, which will recommend list of eligible candidates for Defence Research Technical Cadre 
Central Assessment, based on approved eligibility norms. 


(b) Constitution of Eligibility Screening Committee for Defence Research Technical Cadre Assessment shall 
be as specified in the Sixth Schedule.

(०) Minimum number of years of regular service to be rendered in each grade, for consideration for 
promotion to the next grade shall be as laid down in the Third Schedule. 


(d) Employees in each grade who have rendered the minimum years of regular service as on |“ July of the 
year of assessment shall become eligible for assessment for promotion to next higher grade. 


Note I: Two months relaxation in regular service for promotion to the next grade may be accorded to all existing 
employees who have otherwise completed the minimum laid down regular service as on 0*' September of the year of 
their assessment. 


Note 2: (a) Relaxation upto three months in the minimum regular service for promotion, may be given to all existing 
employees recruited or promoted to their present grade but joined after |‘t September for reasons beyond their control 
and after publication of these rules, such relaxation may be given to those employees recruited or promoted after [7 
July for reasons beyond their control. 


(b) Before granting such relaxation, the Competent Authority shall record the reasons in writing. The 
Competent Authority for this purpose shall be the Chairperson of the Local Assessment Board as mentioned 
in the Fourth Schedule in respect of posts filled through it and Director, Centre for Personnel Talent 
Management in respect of posts filled through Central Assessment Board as mentioned in the Fifth Schedule. 


Note 3: All the employees below the grade of Technical Officer ‘C’ who have rendered five years regular service in 
their grades, after reckoning of relaxations mentioned at Note | and Note 2 above, as on | September, 2025, shall be 
considered for promotion to the next higher grade. 


(2) The period spent on deputation or on foreign service, to a non-technical post, shall not count 
towards required regular service laid down for promotion. 


(3) Period of unauthorised absence and extraordinary leave on personal grounds shall not count as 
qualifying service for eligibility for promotion. However, relaxation of upto three months in required regular 
service for promotion shall be given in the case of an individual availing leave on medical grounds. 


(4) The maximum number of employees in a grade who can be promoted to the next higher grade shall 
be the percentage of the total eligible employees in that grade at each annual assessment as given in the Third 
Schedule subject to the provision of sub-rule (6) of rule 3 and the employees shall be promoted on the basis 
of their overall merit. 


(5) Assessment for promotion to all grades upto grade of Technical Assistant ‘B’ in category-A shall be 
made by a local Assessment Board, the composition of which is given in the Fourth Schedule and the 
assessment for promotion to other grades shall be made by a Central Assessment Board, the composition of 
which is given in the Fifth Schedule. 


6. Effective date of promotion and inter-se seniority on promotion.—(|) Assessments for promotion to each 
grade shall be held once a year and recommendations of the Assessment Board shall be implemented from |“ July of 
the year to which the Assessment Board pertain, except where specific recommendations are made by the Assessment 
Board regarding the date from which the promotion is to take effect. 


(2) Individuals who are on leave on the date of implementation shall assume charge in the grade to 
which they are promoted with effect from the date they resume duty but this shall not affect their date of 
selection or their inter-se seniority in the higher grade vis-a-vis the other individuals cleared for promotion by 
the same Assessment Board. 


(3) Persons assessed and promoted to a grade in an annual assessment shall rank enbloc senior to those 
so assessed and promoted in a subsequent assessment. 


(4) In an annual assessment, individuals promoted from grade of Technical Officer ‘A’ in category-B to 
grade of Technical Officer ‘B’ in category-B shall be placed enbloc senior to the individuals promoted from 
grade of Technical Officer in category-A to grade of Technical Officer ‘B’ in category-B. 


7 Probation.—(|) Every direct recruit to the lowest grades of category-A and category-B, and promotee to the 
grade of Technical Assistant ‘B’ in category-A, and to the grade of Technical Officer “B’ in category-B shall be on 
probation for a period of two years 


Provided that the Controlling Authority may extend the period of probation in accordance with the instructions issued 
by the Government from time to time: 


Provided further that any decision for extension of a probation period shall be taken ordinarily within eight weeks 
after the expiry of the previous probationary period and communicated in writing to the concerned officer together 
with the reasons for so doing within the said period.

(2) On completion of the period of probation or any extension thereof, officers shall, if considered fit 
for permanent appointment, be retained in their appointments on regular basis and be confirmed in due 
course against the available substantive vacancies, as the case may be. 


(3) If, during the period of probation or any extension thereof, as the case may be, Government is of the 
opinion that an officer is not fit for permanent appointment to the grade, Government may discharge or revert 
the officer to the grade held by him prior to his appointment to the said grade, as the case may be. 


(4) During the period of probation, or extension thereof, candidates may be required by the Government 
to undergo such courses of training and instructions and to pass examinations and tests as Government may 
deem fit, as a condition to satisfactory completion of the probation. 


(5) Other matters relating to probation shall be governed by the instructions issued by the Government 
in this regard from time to time. 


8. Nature of duty on promotion.—It shall be obligatory on the part of an individual promoted from one grade 
to another to continue to perform the same duties as he or she was required to perform prior to such promotion if so 
directed by the appointing authority or to perform such other duties as may be assigned to him or her from time to 
time. 


9. Industrial status.—Existing industrial employees shall cease to be industrial employees on promotion to a 
grade in pay level 6 (Rs. 35400-2400) of the pay matrix or higher. 


0. Disqualification.—No person,— 
(a) who has entered into or contracted a marriage with a person having a spouse living; or 
(b) who, having a spouse living, has entered into or contracted a marriage with any person, 


shall be eligible for appointment in the cadre: 


Provided that the Government may, if satisfied that such marriage is permissible under the personal law applicable to 
such persons and the other party to the marriage and that there are other grounds for so doing, exempt any person from 
the operation of this rule. 


i. Power to relax.—Where the Government is of the opinion that it is necessary or expedient so to do, it may, 
by order and for reasons to be recorded in writing, relax any of the provisions of these rules in respect of any class or 
category of persons. 


2. Saving.—Nothing in these rules shall affect reservations and other concessions required to be provided for 
candidates belonging to the Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, Other Backward Classes and other special categories 
of persons in accordance with the orders issued by the Government from time to time in this regard.

S.R.O. 53.—In exercise of the powers conferred by the proviso to article 309 of the Constitution, the
